title: "Assignments"

The course includes five cumulative problem sets. Each problem set develops one focal analysis and asks students to connect that analysis to a linguistic question.

## Problem sets

| Assignment | Linguistic data | Statistical content |
|---|---|---|
| [PS1](../problem-sets/ps1/ps1.qmd) | Hillenbrand vowel acoustics and German UniMorph | frequentist [paired-mean inference](../statistical-inference/paired-mean-inference.qmd), an [exact binomial](../statistical-inference/exact-binomial-intervals.qmd) sign procedure, [Fisher's exact test](../statistical-inference/fishers-exact-test.qmd), [chi-squared inference](../statistical-inference/chi-squared-test.qmd), and empirical sampling distributions across small lexeme samples |
| [PS2](../problem-sets/ps2/ps2.qmd) | Provo Corpus eye movements and UD English EWT | Bayesian [posterior summaries](../statistical-inference/posterior-summaries.qmd), a guided one-dimensional normal–normal conjugacy derivation, the [beta–Bernoulli update](../statistical-inference/conjugate-priors.qmd), scalar beta–binomial association models, and a posterior predictive categorical-independence check |
| [PS3](../problem-sets/ps3/ps3-dative-alternation.qmd) | English dative alternation | [logistic regression](../regression-models/logistic-regression.qmd), leave-one-verb-out evaluation, and a modality boundary-condition analysis |
| [PS4](../problem-sets/ps4/ps4.qmd) | CommitmentBank projection judgments | [ordinal mixed models](../regression-models/ordinal-mixed-models.qmd), prior and posterior checks, and discourse-grouped validation |
| [PS5](../problem-sets/ps5/ps5.qmd) | PHOIBLE phoneme inventories | [singular value decomposition](../factorization/singular-value-decomposition.qmd), balanced held-out reconstruction, and grouped prediction of the first component |

## What students should expect

Each problem set is also an assigned reading. It develops the mathematical background and linguistic motivation before asking students to extend the analysis. The relevant note pages link to the precise problem-set sections that students should read and explain why those sections are included. Students submit the completed notebook and must be prepared to explain the analysis during the in-class assessment.

PS1 and PS2 form a matched pair. They use the same sequence of inferential targets with different linguistic data. PS1 uses Hillenbrand F1 measurements and German UniMorph lexemes. PS2 uses Provo reading times and UD English EWT dependency annotations.

Every numbered task in every problem set is required for every student. The problem sets contain no course-number-specific extensions.
